title: Only, None But and All Except
short: "Only S are P" and "None but S are P" become "All P are S"; "All except S are P" makes two claims.
trouble: Learners keep the order: "Only members may vote" does not say all members vote; it says all voters are members.

blocks.html: Some words in everyday statements change the order of the terms. The most important is only.

"Only S are P" and "None but S are P" become All P are S (swap the terms). "The only S are P" becomes All S are P (keep the order). "All except S are P" makes two claims: All non-S are P, and No S are P.

"Only members may vote" sets a requirement on voters: to vote, you must be a member. That is a claim about every voter: all voters are members. It says nothing about every member; some members may stay home. So the class after "only" is the one the other class must fit inside, and it becomes the predicate. "The only" works the other way: "The only animals in the canyon are skunks" says every animal in the canyon is a skunk.

blocks.name: lg-venn3
blocks.cap: Only members may vote: the part of the voters circle outside the members is empty. Members outside the voters circle are allowed.

head: Everyday wording
Standard form
rows: Only ticket holders are allowed backstage.
All people allowed backstage are ticket holders.
None but seniors may park on campus.
All students who may park on campus are seniors.
The only dogs here are puppies.
All non-seniors are campers, and no seniors are campers.
blocks.cap: Watch the order of the terms.

blocks.title: Only
blocks.q: Put "Only adults may use the hot tub" in standard form.
steps: The class after "only" is the requirement: adults.
Every person who may use the hot tub must be an adult.
blocks.a: All people who may use the hot tub are adults.

blocks.title: All except
blocks.q: Put "All except the drummers are singers" in standard form.
steps: An exceptive makes two claims: one about everyone else, one about the exceptions.
Everyone who is not a drummer is a singer: All non-drummers are singers.
The drummers are the exception: No drummers are singers.
blocks.a: All non-drummers are singers, and no drummers are singers.

blocks.html: Keeping the order of the words. "Only members may vote" does not say that all members vote; it says that all voters are members. Check with a case: picture a member who stays home. Is the rule broken? No, so the rule is not about every member.

sources.name: Patrick J. Hurley, A Concise Introduction to Logic, 4.7 Translating Ordinary Language Statements into Categorical Form (exclusive and exceptive propositions)
